frases: {show m}Can there be a {show m-r0}fine for a book that was {show m-r1}not lent? In our database, {bad m-r1}[-no].
The fine does not point to the member: it points to the {show fkp}{good m-r0 +0.2}[+loan].
The FK is {hl m-h0}loan_id: every fine comes from a [+real] loan.
If that loan does not exist, the fine does not {show e1}[-go] in.
And the loan points to the {show fks}[+member] through member_id.
So only members who took a {show solo}copy can be fined.

elementos.text: Why not an FK straight to member?
It is already implied by the loan
A second path that can contradict it

frases: So why not an {show nov}FK straight to member?
Because it is already {show imp}[+implied], and it would open a second path that could {show dos}[-contradict] it.
A {show r}{show r-r0 +0.2}reservation points to the copy, not the book: {show fkr}{hl r-h0 +0.1}copy_id.
So you reserve one {show una}specific copy, not just any title.
What an FK cannot see, like a copy that is already lent, goes in a {show trg}{boom trg +0.3}[-trigger].
If they ask you, [+say]: FKs {show fl1}in a chain, {show fl2}member, loan, fine, and the database checks it by itself.
{show fnext}Tomorrow: the PK of a copy.
